findings.description: `host.endswith(domain)` has no label boundary, so with partner domain `shop.example` an attacker-controlled origin such as `https://evilshop.example` or `https://attackershop.example` passes `is_allowed`. `response_headers` and `preflight_headers` then echo that origin in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, so a malicious site can make credentialed cross-origin requests to `/v1/balance` and `/v1/redeem` using a logged-in member's session cookie and read the responses.
findings.suggestion: Match on a label boundary: accept when `host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)`, and add a test with a lookalike host such as `evilshop.example`.
findings.title: Partner-domain check matches any host that merely ends with the domain string
